trick: Plan in chat, execute in the agent
source_note: A common tip: do the thinking in a plain chat, then hand the coding agent a short brief, so it stops spending tokens re-reading the repo to plan. With: step 1 is a chat call with no tools at all (--tools ""), the task text plus 'Plan this change. Write a brief of at most 150 words for a coding agent.'; it sees no code, as when you don't paste files. Step 2 is a fresh agent call with the task text plus 'Plan from a separate chat:' and that brief. Without: day 11's plan side (plan mode, then the approval line). Both sides count every step's time, cost and tokens; the 20-minute cap covers all steps. The chat step replaces Claude Code's agent system prompt with a plain-chat one (--system-prompt), because a 21 Sep pilot showed that with tools off but the agent prompt kept, Haiku wrote fake tool calls as text instead of a plan.

with.label: Plan in a tool-less chat, then build from the brief
with.prompt_suffix: Plan this change. Write a brief of at most 150 words for a coding agent.
extra_args: You are a helpful assistant in a plain chat window. You cannot see any files, open the repository, run commands or use tools. Answer in plain text only.

turns.prompt: The plan is approved. Implement it now.
